title: A front-desk login can give any member door access with any end date, paid or not
what: When entry machines are on, the admin app works out each member's door dates from their plan and sends them to the server to pass on to the door machines. The server accepts these orders from any front-desk login and checks only that the member number belongs to the gym. It never checks the dates against the member's real plan. A desk login that sends its own order (for example from the browser's developer tools) can switch a lapsed member on, or give them no end date at all. The server already stops the desk from handing out free months in the member records, so this is a way round that rule.
expected: The server works out a member's door dates from the saved plan itself, or refuses a desk order whose dates go beyond the member's paid plan.
how_often: only if a desk login sends its own order; entry machines are behind a switch
fix_line: Let the server set door dates from the saved plan instead of taking them from the browser

title: No test proves another gym is refused when editing, hiding or re-photographing a product, reading the app members list, or saving alert settings
what: Each of these calls works out the gym from the sign-in key and only touches that gym's rows, so reading the code found no leak. But the database tests never try them with a second gym's key. The access test table covers listing, restocking and deleting a product, not editing, hiding or changing its photo. The app members list (names and mobile numbers of members who joined from the app) has no test of its own at all, only a line saying it may be called without signing in. Alert settings are tested with this gym's owner and desk only, though a second gym's key is made in the same test. A later change that broke the gym check would not be caught.
expected: For each of these calls, a database test uses a second gym's owner key against the first gym's product, members and settings and checks that it is refused or sees nothing.
how_often: only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add second-gym refusal checks for these calls to the database tests

items.reason: 94 database calls, all open to the app key and each checked by the sign-in key: owner-only calls (products, branding, rename, messages, billing, pay MettleUp, entry machine add/remove) refuse the desk; orders, member photos, measurements, WOD and machine numbers are open to any staff login by design. Server routes: billing checkout is owner-only on the server; the push key and link address are public by design.

Every table the area reaches has row rules on and no rule letting apps in (only the gyms read rule and the photo upload rules exist); all access is through key-checked calls. Second-gym refusal tests found for orders, product list/restock/delete, brand, rename, messages, member photos, measurements, diet, offers, reminders, plan requests, phone links, WOD, questions, member messages, alerts, timings, pay MettleUp, receipts.

Product edit/hide/photo, app members list, alert settings: new finding. Busy machines, Bring a friend, leaderboard, entry machines: already FN-L3-panel-screens-1-01. Personal training and browser alerts: already FN-L3-server-database-3-04.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run.
No key pattern hits in the area; the only fixed address is the public photo storage address, not a secret.
No AI or payment key in this area: the push key fetched is the public half by design; checkout sends only the sign-in key to our own server.
The area keeps the sign-in key in the browser with no end date; already found. PIN reset and wrong-try limits live in the sign-in area, not here.
No raw HTML in the area (all text drawn by React or onto a canvas); product text has length limits in the table; logo and photo addresses must match our own storage pattern. No fault found.

Photos are re-drawn as JPEG in the browser (drops hidden photo data); bucket takes only JPEG/PNG/WebP under 3 MB; ticket is owner-only. The ticket can be reused for 15 minutes though the code calls it one-time: already found.
Invite, join-online and check-in links are all built from the gym's join code, which can be found by trying codes: already found.
The area uses only react, the database client, qrcode-generator and the shared theme; none is on the known-flaw list. Repo-wide gap (no ongoing scan) already found.
